fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people? Read More Universal Design Playground Play is a fundamental aspect of human development that continues all through our lives. Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but many individuals struggle to fully engage in these spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often, playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of play or particular age groups, which can leave children who cannot participate in the intended manner feeling excluded. For children with disabilities, play is even more crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social skills. However, the conventional design of playgrounds does not typically accommodate their needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit to a standard playground with children with disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design that fail to satisfy everyone. Playgrounds should be designed to foster social connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation, encourage physical exercise, and connect with nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging design task. By involving children with disabilities and their families in the design process and creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge that play is more than just a source of enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the joy of play. For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants. Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.

questions.passage: Universal design suggests that design be as (A)[flexible / rigid] as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a (B)[wide / narrow] range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more (C)[common / rare] types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① flexible(유연한)+wide(넓은)+common(흔한): 유니버설 디자인은 다양한 요구를 수용하도록 '유연'해야 하고, '넓은' 범위의 개인 취향을 담으며, 보통의 가위·마우스는 '흔한' 종류라는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② rigid(경직된)는 가능한 한 유연해야 한다는 설명과 정반대
❌ ③ narrow(좁은)는 '넓은' 범위의 취향을 수용한다는 흐름과 반대
❌ ④ rare(드문)는 '흔한' 종류의 제품과 대비한다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: flexible=유연한, wide=넓은, common=흔한

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is (A)[accessible / restricted] to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be (B)[excluded / included]. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts (C)[eliminate / create] barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① restricted(제한된)는 모두가 '이용할 수 있게' 한다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② accessible(접근 가능한)+excluded(배제된)+eliminate(없애다): 환경·제품이 모두에게 '접근 가능'해야 하고, 누구도 '배제'되어선 안 되며, 연석 경사로가 장벽을 '없앤다'는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ included(포함된)는 누구도 배제되면 안 된다는 흐름과 어긋남(should be included가 아니라 not excluded)
❌ ④ create(만들다)는 장벽을 '없앤다'는 문맥과 정반대
det.tip: accessible=접근 가능한, excluded=배제된, eliminate=없애다

questions.passage: Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a (A)[weak / strong] grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a (B)[closed / open] hand, which (C)[benefits / harms] people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① strong(강한)은 뚜껑 열기가 힘든 대상이 '약한' 악력을 가진 사람이라는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② open(펼친)은 '쥔(closed) 손'으로도 문을 열 수 있다는 예시와 반대
✅ ③ weak(약한)+closed(쥔)+benefits(이롭게 하다): '약한' 악력의 사람에게 뚜껑 열기가 어렵고, 레버형 손잡이는 '쥔' 손이나 팔꿈치로도 열려 손 힘이 약한 사람에게 '이롭다'는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ④ harms(해롭게 하다)는 사람들에게 '이롭다'는 글의 결론과 반대
det.tip: weak=약한, closed=(주먹 쥔) 닫힌, benefits=이롭게 하다

det.korean: ④ easy → difficult: 왼손잡이 도구가 없으면 사용하기 '어렵다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① diverse: 서로 다른 사람들의 '다양한' 요구를 고려한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② accommodate: '다양한' 요구를 '수용한다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ common: 왼손잡이용이 일반적인 '흔한' 종류와 어떻게 다른지 묻는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ easy → difficult: 그런 도구가 '없으면(Without them)' 왼손잡이는 단순한 제품도 사용하기 '어렵다(difficult)'가 맞다. easy는 정반대 ← 정답
det.tip: difficult(어려운) ↔ easy(쉬운)

det.korean: ③ harder → easier: 보편 기호를 찾으면 화장실 찾기가 더 '쉬워진다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① critical: '중요한' 정보가 잘 전달되도록 하는 디자인이라는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② written: 정보를 '문자 언어'뿐 아니라 기호·음성으로도 전달한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ harder → easier: 현지어를 해석하는 대신 보편적 화장실 기호를 찾으면 화장실 찾기가 훨씬 '쉬워진다(easier)'가 맞다. harder는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ confirm: 음성 안내가 선택된 층을 '확인해 준다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: easier(더 쉬운) ↔ harder(더 어려운)

questions.passage: Curb cuts ①<u>create</u> barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.  Like curb cuts, ②<u>automatic</u> doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems.  Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① create → eliminate: 연석 경사로(curb cuts)는 휠체어 이용자뿐 아니라 무거운 짐을 옮기거나 자전거를 타는 사람의 장벽을 '없앤다(eliminate)'가 맞다. create(만들다)는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ② automatic: 공공건물의 '자동' 문이 모두를 들어가게 한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ comfortably: 제품을 효율적이고 '편안하게' 쓸 수 있게 한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ clever: 뚜껑을 여는 다양한 '기발한' 장치들이 만들어졌다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: eliminate(없애다) ↔ create(만들다)

det.tip: a fundamental aspect of human development(근본적인 측면) ↔ trivial(사소한)

questions.passage:
(A) Universal design can accommodate a wide <u>range</u> of individual preferences and abilities. A height-adjustable desk, for example, suits many different users at once.
(B) The mountain <u>range</u> in the distance was covered with snow all winter. Its highest peaks were far too steep to climb.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 range의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) a wide range of preferences는 취향의 '범위·폭'을 뜻하고, (B) mountain range는 눈 덮인 '산맥'을 뜻함 ← 정답
❌ ① (A)는 '산맥'이 아니라 취향의 범위
❌ ③ (A)는 '사격장'이 아니라 범위
❌ ④ (B)는 '다양성'이 아니라 산맥
det.tip: range: (A) (취향의) 범위·폭 / (B) 산맥

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a condition that makes a part of a person's body or mind not work fully"

det.analysis:
❌ ① symbol: 상징, 기호
❌ ② preference: 선호, 취향
❌ ③ device: 장치, 기구
✅ ④ impairment: 신체나 정신의 일부가 온전히 기능하지 못하는 상태(장애) ← 정답
det.tip: people with visual or audio impairments = 시각·청각 장애가 있는 사람 → impairment = 장애

questions.passage: Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or __________ (add) adjustable features to a product.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: add(동사 원형) → adding(동명사): 앞의 providing과 or로 나란히 이어지는 자리다. involve의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 providing과 형태를 맞춰야 하므로 adding(동명사)이 맞다. providing ... or adding(제공하거나 추가하는 것).
det.tip: involve + 동명사, providing ... or ___ : and/or로 이어지는 병렬은 같은 형태(동명사)로 → adding

questions.passage: Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without __________ (cause) unnecessary fatigue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: cause(동사 원형) → causing(동명사): 전치사 without 뒤에는 목적어로 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. without causing unnecessary fatigue(불필요한 피로를 유발하지 않고서)가 맞으므로 causing으로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: 전치사(without) + 동명사(-ing): without causing(유발하지 않으면서)

questions.passage: Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone.  Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded.  Curb cuts are a good example.  Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city.  Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes.  Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 without any major problems(별다른 문제 없이)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① without any major problems(별다른 문제 없이): 자동문은 연석 경사로처럼 모든 사람이 '별 문제 없이' 건물에 들어가게 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ② at a fixed cost(정해진 비용으로): 비용은 이 글의 논점이 아님
❌ ③ in a special order(특별한 순서로): 순서와 무관
❌ ④ with expert help(전문가의 도움으로): 스스로 접근 가능하게 한다는 취지와 반대
det.tip: allow all people to enter without any major problems: 모두가 별 문제 없이 들어가게 하다

questions.passage: For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground.  Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child.  The various methods of play have __________, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top.  Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground.  The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants.  Play isn’t just for kids anymore.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 different means of access(서로 다른 접근 수단)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① the same entrance fee(같은 입장료): 비용 이야기가 아님
❌ ② a single fixed path(단 하나의 고정된 길): 언덕을 오르거나 경사로를 쓰는 등 '여러' 방법이 있다는 뒤 내용과 반대
✅ ③ different means of access(서로 다른 접근 수단): 언덕을 기어오르는 아이도, 걷지 못하는 아이도 경사로로 정상에 이르는 등 놀이 방식마다 '서로 다른 접근 수단'이 있다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ no safety rules(안전 규칙 없음): 접근 방식과 무관
det.tip: different means of access, allowing kids who ... while children who can't walk ...: 서로 다른 접근 수단
